items.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I orchestrated an album for the pop band Chicago because the co-leader, Jim Panko, the trombone player is a big Bill Watrous fan

ctx.x: You mentioned writing for Hollywood and the studios. How did that come about? Do you need to meet people? Is there a way like —

My standard line is it’s a business of relationships, and all it takes is one. That’s another interesting thing is when you read interviews of film composers, well I was playing in some rock band and so-and-so became a fan and I did their student film and then they made it, and I mean it’s never I graduated from film scoring school and made phone calls and I got hired. Or they came and recruited me like lawyers. It’s totally relationships. Every cool job I’ve ever gotten has been from some convoluted path. And…
Is it a high pressure situation, writing for films?
